analysis: The code snippet calls `certs[i].getEncoded()` inside a loop. The method `getEncoded()` is documented to throw `CertificateEncodingException` if an encoding error occurs. The calling context does not perform any validation or check on the certificate before calling `getEncoded()`. There is no null check on `certs` or its elements, nor any attempt to handle the exception within this line. The method `dumpCertInfo` itself declares `throws CertificateEncodingException`, so the exception can propagate. Therefore, the throwing condition of `CertificateEncodingException` is not avoided by any checks or validations in the snippet.
remark: The exception `CertificateEncodingException` can be triggered if the certificate's encoded form cannot be generated due to encoding issues. This can occur if the certificate object is malformed, the underlying data is corrupted, or if the certificate type does not support the encoding format (though for X.509 it is generally ASN.1 DER). The code does not include any preventive checks, so the exception may be thrown during the call `certs[i].getEncoded()`.
